metadata.title: FrontlineAI - Set 2: Scenario-Based RAG Test Questions & Answers
metadata.subtitle: Papua New Guinea / WHO benchmark with mixed answerable and deliberately unanswerable items
metadata.purpose: Evaluation set for RAG grounding tests. Includes clinically answerable questions from the 14 supplied documents and deliberately unanswerable questions where the corpus lacks authoritative guidance. A correct system should cite sources for answerable items and refuse or state uncertainty for unanswerable ones.
metadata.design: Fifty topics x two scenario templates = 100 questions. Scenario templates differ from Set 1: night_shift_worker, parent_counselling, referral_decision, and doctor_on_call. Unanswerable items use category 'Unanswerable' and source_of_truth 'Not in corpus.'
metadata.source_hierarchy: 1) Newer PNG/WHO updates for the exact topic; 2) PNG national standard-treatment guidance for local practice; 3) WHO technical guidance; 4) older PNG textbooks mainly as supporting context. The older 2003 paediatrics text was not allowed to override later treatment guidance.

questions.question: On night shift at the health centre, I encounter this situation: Uncomplicated malaria ACT treatment. What should I do according to the guideline?
questions.answer: For uncomplicated malaria with a positive malaria test (or when testing is unavailable) and no severe signs, give ACT (Co-artem/MALA), paracetamol if temperature is 38°C or higher, treat other causes of fever if present, continue treatment at home, and review if fever persists.

questions.question: A worried parent asks me about Uncomplicated malaria ACT treatment. What is the correct guidance I should give?
questions.answer: For uncomplicated malaria with a positive malaria test (or when testing is unavailable) and no severe signs, give ACT (Co-artem/MALA), paracetamol if temperature is 38°C or higher, treat other causes of fever if present, continue treatment at home, and review if fever persists.

questions.question: On night shift at the health centre, I encounter this situation: Rabies status in PNG. What should I do according to the guideline?
